indicators.name: Areas under restoration actions (Ecuador module)
indicators.description_short: Government inventory of areas under restoration actions inside the Ecuadorian Amazon module, with modality, practice, implementer, funding and year.
indicators.description:
### Areas under restoration actions

Government inventory of areas where restoration activities are implemented to recover conditions favouring natural processes and the maintenance of environmental services. It is an inventory of interventions, not a wall-to-wall classification of the territory.

### Data source & methodology

Ministry of Environment and Energy, IDE Ambiente geoportal, Environmental Management / Forest Restoration. Source object TB002, geographic information dated December 2025. Redundant Z dimension removed, 17 invalid geometries repaired, clipped by intersection with ECU_MOD, reprojected to WGS 84 (EPSG:4326). No simplification. Area_ha recalculated after clipping.

### Specific content of the layer

Object and agreement codes, beneficiary code, implementer, restoration modality and practice, funding origin, year of intervention, recalculated area and an added short thematic description.

### Technical details

5,831 source records, 5,082 inside ECU_MOD, 17,404.305 ha (174.043 km²). By modality: 3,686 active restoration (72.53%) and 1,396 passive (27.47%). Extent W -79.306573, S -4.710554, E -76.612927, N 0.116707.

### References & access links

IDE Ambiente geoportal; official dictionary TB002.

indicators.name: Restoration priority areas (Ecuador module)
indicators.description_short: Very high, High, Medium and Low priority classes for forest restoration inside the Ecuadorian Amazon module.
indicators.description:
### Restoration priority areas

Derived from the official "Área prioritaria de restauración" product. The source describes these as suitable, potential or optimal zones meeting the natural and social characteristics needed for forest restoration interventions.

### Data source & methodology

Ministry of Environment and Energy, IDE Ambiente geoportal. Thematic code TB001, geographic information dated 2016. Spatial selection by ECU_MOD, dissolve by priority class, exact clip, area calculation and reprojection to WGS 84 (EPSG:4326). Empty source fields were removed; priority values normalised to sentence case.

### Specific content of the layer

Four multipart geometries, one per priority class, with recalculated area in hectares and square kilometres and a short per-class description. The class descriptions express only the relative hierarchy of the source attribute: the public ficha defines the set of priority areas but gives no separate textual definition or threshold per level.

### Technical details

268,864 source polygons reduced to 4 records by dissolve, without thematic reclassification. Total 1,495,775.770 ha (14,957.758 km²): Very high 369,274.691 ha, High 744,165.351 ha, Medium 169,210.929 ha, Low 213,124.799 ha.

### References & access links

IDE Ambiente geoportal; National Forest Monitoring System; REDD+ Ecuador, Forest Conservation and Restoration.

indicators.name: Bioclimates (Ecuador module)
indicators.description_short: Bioclimatic classes present in the Ecuadorian Amazon module, classified by temperature and precipitation.
indicators.description:
### Bioclimates

Bioclimatic classification of the Ecuadorian Amazon module according to temperature and precipitation. It is one of the factors underlying the national ecosystem cartography, alongside thermotypes, geomorphology and biogeographic units.

### Data source & methodology

Ministry of Environment and Energy, IDE Ambiente geoportal, source component GE003. Dissolve by bioclimate followed by clipping to ECU_MOD. Internal code, source area and associated text removed. Final CRS WGS 84 (EPSG:4326).

### Specific content of the layer

Bioclimate class and the recalculated area in hectares.

### Technical details

800 source polygons, 3 final classes inside ECU_MOD.

### References & access links

IDE Ambiente geoportal; official dictionary GE003_BIOCLIMA.

caveats.text: Carbono_t_ha is the mean carbon stock of each forest stratum in tonnes per hectare, not a measurement per polygon. Total carbon for an area is not computed by this service.

indicators.name: Deforestation 2020-2022 (Ecuador module)
indicators.description_short: Gross deforestation 2020-2022 in the Ecuadorian Amazon module, as land cover transition trajectories from forest to other covers.
indicators.description:
### Deforestation 2020-2022

Component FC010 of the IDE Ambiente geoportal. It represents gross deforestation through land cover change trajectories, from forest towards other covers, for the 2020-2022 period.

### Data source & methodology

Ministry of Environment and Energy, IDE Ambiente geoportal, source FC010. National dissolve by Period + Transition, followed by clipping to ECU_MOD. Code, source area and associated text removed; Area_ha recalculated after clipping. Final CRS WGS 84 (EPSG:4326).

### Specific content of the layer

Period, transition class and recalculated area. Because the dissolve is by Period + Transition, each record is a multipart geometry aggregating all patches of one transition class, not an individual deforestation event.

### Technical details

50,424 source polygons reduced to 8 final classes, confirmed against the live service.

### References & access links

IDE Ambiente geoportal, https://ide.ambiente.gob.ec/mapainteractivo/ and the documentation supplied with the delivery.

indicators.name: Hydrographic Demarcations (Ecuador module)
indicators.description_short: The three Hydrographic Demarcations of Ecuador that intersect the Amazon module: administrative territorial units for water management.
indicators.description:
### Hydrographic Demarcations

Administrative territorial divisions for water management corresponding to Ecuador's Hydrographic Demarcations that intersect the Amazon module. They are administrative units built on watersheds, not the watersheds themselves.

### Data source & methodology

Ministry of Environment and Energy, IDE Ambiente geoportal, source HB003, an institutional water planning reference. Only the demarcation name and the clipped area are retained. The fcode and ralt attributes were discarded: the first is an internal code and the second has no documented definition in the received package, so it is not exposed to users. No dissolve or simplification.

### Specific content of the layer

Demarcation name and recalculated area in hectares.

### Technical details

10 national polygons in the source; 3 intersect ECU_MOD, confirmed by querying the live service. Note that the aggregated project metadata previously stated eight demarcations; that figure was wrong.

### References & access links

IDE Ambiente geoportal, https://ide.ambiente.gob.ec/mapainteractivo/ ; Sistema Único de Información Ambiental.

indicators.name: Ecosystems (Ecuador module)
indicators.description_short: The 51 ecosystem classes present in the Ecuadorian Amazon module, from the Ecosystem Map of Continental Ecuador (characterised for 2012).
indicators.description:
### Ecosystems

Vector component derived from the official Ecosystem cartography of Continental Ecuador. The source characterises ecosystems as of 2012 and was published as geographic information in 2013, at 1:100,000 scale, using biophysical modelling, interpretation of 2010-2012 satellite imagery and field validation.

This layer is not a wall-to-wall land cover and use map. Areas without a polygon are not a category called "non-ecosystem" and are not equivalent to "non-forest"; transformed surfaces or anthropic uses must be read from a dedicated land cover component.

### Data source & methodology

Ministry of Environment and Energy, IDE Ambiente / Interactive Map. 790 invalid geometries in the ECU_MOD calculation extent were repaired, precision was reduced to a common 90 m grid (three steps of the original 30 m grid), and patches were dissolved by ecosystem code. Thematic attributes are constant per ecosystem code, so the dissolve removes record fragmentation without removing thematic variation. Exact clip by ECU_MOD, reprojection to WGS 84 (EPSG:4326), geodesic area recalculated last.

### Specific content of the layer

Ecosystem code and name, ecosystem type, physiognomy, fragility, threat, vulnerability, fragmentation, connectivity, and area in hectares and square kilometres. Fragility, threat, vulnerability, fragmentation and connectivity are source attributes; the processing does not recalculate or update them.

### Technical details

91,347 source polygons, 87 ecosystem codes, EPSG:32717. Inside ECU_MOD: 51 classes (36 forest, 6 shrubland, 9 herbaceous physiognomy; 48 terrestrial, 3 aquatic types), 10,767,901.75 ha / 107,679.02 km², 2,533,992 vertices, 0 invalid geometries. Area variation from the generalisation step was about -0.00108%. For patch boundaries at source resolution, use the original ZIP.

### References & access links

Official dictionary GE000_ECOSISTEMA; IDE Ambiente Interactive Map, https://ide.ambiente.gob.ec/mapainteractivo/

indicators.name: Geomorphology (Ecuador module)
indicators.description_short: The 53 geomorphological units of the Ecuadorian Amazon module, with the hierarchy Relief – Macrorelief – Mesorelief.
indicators.description:
### Geomorphology

Hierarchical classification of landforms in the Ecuadorian Amazon module. It is one of the factors underlying the national ecosystem cartography, alongside bioclimates, thermotypes and biogeographic units.

### Data source & methodology

Ministry of Environment and Energy, IDE Ambiente geoportal, source GE004. The Relief–Macrorelief–Mesorelief hierarchy is preserved and a dissolve by thematic combination is applied, yielding multipart units. Empty name, internal code, source area and associated text are excluded. Final CRS WGS 84 (EPSG:4326).

### Specific content of the layer

Relief, macrorelief, mesorelief and recalculated area in hectares.

### Technical details

23,374 source polygons; 995 intersect ECU_MOD; 53 multipart units after the dissolve, confirmed against the live service.

### References & access links

IDE Ambiente geoportal and the official documentation supplied with the delivery.

indicators.name: Flooding Regime (Ecuador module)
indicators.description_short: Floodability zones and water origin in the Ecuadorian Amazon module. Floodability is a vegetation descriptor, not a hazard assessment.
indicators.description:
### Flooding Regime

The official GE005 dictionary defines floodability as the capacity for saturation and permanence of water sufficient to influence the structure and composition of vegetation.

### Interpretation note

This is an ecological descriptor of vegetation cover, not a model of flood hazard or risk. It must not be presented or queried as a hazard layer.

### Data source & methodology

Ministry of Environment and Energy, IDE Ambiente geoportal, source GE005. Attributes were cleaned and geometries clipped exactly to ECU_MOD. No dissolve was applied in this version because the cover has a complex topology and merging by class is not stable without altering the geometry; spatial fidelity was prioritised. Final CRS WGS 84 (EPSG:4326).

### Specific content of the layer

Flooding regime, water origin and recalculated area in hectares.

### Technical details

15,034 source polygons; 14,137 intersect ECU_MOD, confirmed against the live service. This is the highest feature count in the Ecuador module after layer 03, so the absence of a dissolve is a deliberate performance-versus-fidelity trade-off.

### References & access links

IDE Ambiente geoportal and the documentation supplied with the delivery.

indicators.name: Thermotypes (Ecuador module)
indicators.description_short: The 11 thermotypic classes present in the Ecuadorian Amazon module, related to annual maximum, minimum and mean temperatures.
indicators.description:
### Thermotypes

Thermotypic classification related to annual maximum, minimum and mean temperatures. It is one of the factors underlying the national ecosystem cartography, alongside bioclimates, geomorphology and biogeographic units.

### Data source & methodology

Ministry of Environment and Energy, IDE Ambiente geoportal, source GE002. Dissolve by thermotype before clipping to ECU_MOD. Internal code, source area and associated text removed. Final CRS WGS 84 (EPSG:4326).

### Specific content of the layer

Thermotype class and recalculated area in hectares.

### Technical details

3,585 source polygons, 11 classes present in ECU_MOD, confirmed against the live service.

### References & access links

IDE Ambiente geoportal, https://ide.ambiente.gob.ec/mapainteractivo/

indicators.name: Climate Types (Ecuador module)
indicators.description_short: The six climate types present in the Ecuadorian Amazon module, from the national climate classification.
indicators.description:
### Climate Types

Polygon vector component representing the climate types present in the Ecuadorian Amazon module. It is the national-resolution counterpart of the regional Climate Zones indicator.

### Data source & methodology

Historical provenance MAGAP–SIGAGRO, via the agriculture geoportal. The operational source is the tipos_clima shapefile preserved in the delivery; the exact WFS URL, typeName and download date were not recorded and are unavailable. Original CRS EPSG:32717. Attribute text normalised to sentence case with correct accents, climate codes preserved, national dissolve by climate class, reprojection to WGS 84 (EPSG:4326), clip by ECU_MOD, a further dissolve after clipping and geodesic recalculation of AREA_HA.

### Specific content of the layer

Climate code, climate type and recalculated area. Note that this layer's field names are upper-case (COD_CLIMA, TIPO_CLIMA, AREA_HA), unlike every other layer in the Ecuador module.

### Technical details

6 classes inside ECU_MOD, confirmed against the live service: Af megathermal rainy 78,994.97 km²; Aw tropical megathermal humid 19,450.61 km²; Cb equatorial mesothermal dry 1,134.15 km²; Ch equatorial mesothermal semi-humid 16,248.82 km²; N nival 1,073.06 km²; Pf equatorial high mountain 14,485.57 km². This layer has the weakest provenance of the module: the WFS trail is lost and no source date is recorded.

### References & access links

Historical portal https://geoportal.agricultura.gob.ec/ ; exact WFS endpoint not available.

indicators.name: Biogeographic Units (Ecuador module)
indicators.description_short: The 11 biogeographic units intersecting the Ecuadorian Amazon module, organised as region, biogeographic province and sector.
indicators.description:
### Biogeographic Units

Component that organises the territory into biogeographic regions, provinces and sectors. It is the national-resolution counterpart of the regional Biome Types indicator and places the module's ecosystems in their regional biogeographic context.

### Data source & methodology

Ministry of Environment and Energy, IDE Ambiente geoportal, source GE006. Region, biogeographic province and biogeographic sector are preserved; internal code and associated text removed. No dissolve. Final CRS WGS 84 (EPSG:4326).

### Specific content of the layer

Region, biogeographic province, biogeographic sector and recalculated area in hectares. The province field name is truncated to Provincia_ by the Shapefile 10-character field limit.

### Technical details

19 units in the source; 11 intersect ECU_MOD, confirmed against the live service.

### References & access links

IDE Ambiente geoportal and the official documentation supplied with the delivery.

indicators.name: Water Recharge Zone (Ecuador module)
indicators.description_short: Water recharge zone clipped to the Ecuadorian Amazon module: territory able to retain, store and provide water resources.
indicators.description:
### Water Recharge Zone

Polygon component representing the Water Recharge Zone distributed by Ecuador's IDE Ambiente geoportal. The official ficha describes these zones as territories that, by their intrinsic characteristics, location and environmental conditions, are able to retain, store and provide water resources.

### Data source & methodology

Geoportal IDE Ambiente of the Ministry of Environment of Ecuador, component "Zona de Recarga Hídrica", geographic information dated November 2021. The ECU_MOD polygon was temporarily transformed to the original CRS so the intersection could be computed in projected coordinates; spatial clip by intersection, without generalisation or simplification; reprojection to WGS 84 (EPSG:4326); attribute table normalised to readable Spanish; the original value "ZRH Cuenca" expanded to "Zona de recarga hídrica de cuenca"; area recalculated in hectares and square kilometres; a short Descrip field added from the geoportal ficha.

### Specific content of the layer

Normalised zone name, area in hectares and square kilometres, and a short conceptual description. The component is monothematic and can be drawn with a single polygon symbol.

### Technical details

One valid multipart geometry. Source area 191,937.563 ha (1,919.376 km²); final area after clipping 151,295.043 ha (1,512.950 km²). Extent W -79.364167, S -3.172773, E -78.888517, N -2.600304. Feature count of 1 confirmed against the live service, so any per-feature aggregation returns a single value.

### References & access links

IDE Ambiente geoportal, https://ide.ambiente.gob.ec/mapainteractivo/ ; derived ECU_MOD product prepared August 2026.

indicators.name: Slope
indicators.description:
### Slope Classes Indicator

This raster layer has been developed to represent **terrain slope indicators** based on the **Copernicus DEM GLO-30** digital elevation model, providing a detailed classification of the topographic characteristics of the Earth's surface.

### Data source & methodology

The data comes from **Copernicus DEM**, managed by the **European Space Agency (ESA)** as part of the European Union's Copernicus program. Specifically, the **GLO-30** product was used, which offers global coverage altimetry with a **spatial resolution of 30 meters**. Processing was performed to generate a categorical slope classification based on degree inclination ranges.

### Applications & benefits

-   **Territorial planning:** Identification of areas suitable for urban development and infrastructure
-   **Risk analysis:** Assessment of susceptibility to landslides and erosion
-   **Environmental conservation:** Identification of protection areas and ecological corridors
-   **Agriculture:** Determination of areas suitable for crops according to slope
-   **Forest management:** Planning of forest activities and accessibility

### Specific content of the layer

The layer classifies slope into **7 main categories:**

-   **0° - 1°:** Flat, plains, floodplains
-   **1° - 5°:** Undulating, gently sloping
-   **5° - 15°:** Very undulating, steeply sloping
-   **15° - 30°:** Strongly undulating, steep
-   **30° - 45°:** Very steep, inaccessible on foot
-   **45° - 60°:** Steep, abrupt
-   **60° - 90°:** Very steep, rocky walls

### Technical details

**Spatial resolution:** 30 meters\
**Geographic coverage:** Global\
**Data type:** Categorical raster\
**Base source:** Copernicus DEM GLO-30\
**Classification method:** Slope degree ranges

### References & access links

**Data access:** European Space Agency (ESA). (2023). Copernicus Contributing Missions: Collections Description. Copernicus Contributing Missions Portal. Available at: <https://dataspace.copernicus.eu/explore-data/data-collections/copernicus-contributing-missions/collections-description/COP-DEM>

**Methodological reference:** Fahrland, E., Iavarone, M., & Borla, M. (2022). Evolution of the Copernicus DEM: going beyond today's elevation data. VH-RODA 2022. Available at: <https://earth.esa.int/eogateway/documents/20142/4139742/2.16_VH-RODA%202022%20-%20CopernicusDEM%20Evolution-%20EFahrland.pdf>

indicators.name: Land cover
indicators.description:
### **Land Cover Classes in the Amazon**

This layer is a custom compilation by *AmazoniaForever360+*, based on data from the *ESA WorldCover* project. This product consists of a global land cover dataset with a **10-meter spatial resolution for the year 2021**. The original data was generated using images from the **Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 satellites**, combining optical and radar data.

-   **Sentinel-1** provides **synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data**, which is independent of weather conditions.
-   **Sentinel-2** offers **high-resolution multispectral imagery**, enabling precise and detailed land cover classification.

The project was developed by a consortium of European research institutions and service providers, led by **VITO (Vlaamse Instelling voor Technologisch Onderzoek)**, with contributions from **Brockmann Consult, CS Group, GAMMA Remote Sensing, the International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis (IIASA), and Wageningen University (WUR).**

### **Applications & Benefits**

This dataset serves as a **baseline reference** for land cover types such as forests, wetlands, and human-altered areas. It helps:

-   **Assess land-use changes**
-   **Identify critical biodiversity areas**
-   **Support environmental planning & sustainable resource management**

Its high resolution and accuracy facilitate **informed decision-making** for **conservation initiatives, climate change mitigation, and balanced socio-economic development**.

### **Land Cover Classes**

This layer includes **11 land cover categories**:

1.  Tree Cover
2.  Shrubland
3.  Grassland
4.  Cropland
5.  Built-up Areas
6.  Bare/Sparse Vegetation
7.  Snow & Ice
8.  Permanent Water Bodies
9.  Herbaceous Wetlands
10. Mangroves
11. Moss & Lichens

The **global accuracy of the 2021 map is 76.7%**, independently validated. The original data was downloaded as **10°x10° tiles** and compiled into a thematic raster mosaic covering the **Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) area of operations**. To enhance visualization, the data was **resampled to a 250-meter resolution**.

### **WorldCover Project**

The *WorldCover* project is led by the **Earth Observation Department of the European Space Agency (ESA)** and is part of the **ESA Climate Change Initiative**. The dataset was published in **2021** and is backed by a rigorous scientific methodology detailed in multiple sources.

### **Access to Data & Documentation**

-   **WorldCover Data Download:**\
    <https://worldcover2021.esa.int/>

-   **WorldCover Viewer:**\
    <https://viewer.esa-worldcover.org/worldcover/>

-   **User Manual & Documentation:**\
    <https://worldcover2021.esa.int/documents>

-   **Main Reference on Methodology:**\
    **Zanaga, D., et al. (2021). ESA WorldCover 10 m 2020 V100, European Space Agency.**\
    DOI: <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5571936>

indicators.name: Forest Cover
indicators.description_short: Forest cover analysis, percentage per 1km² grid cell (GLAD 2024)
indicators.description:
## **AMAZONIA FOREST COVER 2024**
Amazonian forest cover map for 2024 derived from Hansen/UMD (GLAD) global forest change data.

### **Data Source & Methodology**

-   **Source:** *UMD/hansen/global_forest_change_2024_v1_12* (GLAD, University of Maryland).

-   **Platform:** Google Earth Engine (GEE).

-   **Spatial resolution:** 30 m (original) → 1 km (aggregated).

-   **Processing steps:**

    1.  Computed tree cover fraction for year 2000 as baseline.

    2.  Applied forest loss and gain (2000--2024) layers.

    3.  Followed Hansen's suggested methodology:

        -   **All deforestation** events between 2000 and 2024 were considered.

        -   **Reforestation** was only counted when detected in 30 m pixels showing *continuous regrowth* without any previous or subsequent deforestation.

        -   Hansen emphasizes that reforestation is a long-term process (> 20 years) and cannot yet be easily or reliably identified from optical imagery alone.

    4.  Computations were performed at 30 m resolution and then **upscaled to 1 km** by aggregating the percentage of forested 30 m pixels within each 1 km cell.

    5.  Final map expresses **forest cover (%) in 2024** per 1 km grid cell.

### **Google Earth Engine (GEE) Methodology**

All operations were conducted using a custom GEE script:

-   Data imported directly from the Hansen GLAD catalog.

-   Boolean masks and temporal filters applied for gain/loss analysis.

-   Aggregation and export steps implemented with GEE reducers (`ee.Reducer.mean()` and `ee.Image.reduceResolution()`).

-   Outputs validated visually and through area comparison with reference datasets.

### **Data Sources & Limitations**

-   Based on optical Landsat imagery; cloud cover and temporal gaps may affect some areas.

-   Hansen dataset provides consistent annual updates but lacks precise timing for reforestation events.

-   The 30 m to 1 km aggregation reduces spatial detail but allows regional comparison and integration with climatic or socio-economic data.

### **Applications & Benefits**

-   Monitoring deforestation and regrowth dynamics.

-   Supporting conservation and territorial planning.

-   Estimating carbon and biodiversity changes.

### **Specific Content of the Layer**

-   **forest_in_2024_P:** Forest cover 2024 (%).

### **References & Access Links**

-   Dataset: `UMD/hansen/global_forest_change_2024_v1_12`

-   Documentation: <https://glad.umd.edu/dataset/global-forest-change>

indicators.name: Grassland Coverage Classes
indicators.description:
## Grassland Coverage Classes Layer

Thematic raster layer representing the extent of different grassland classes from the Global Pasture Watch (GPW) model. Grasslands are ecosystems dominated by perennial and annual herbaceous plants, mainly grasses, with little or no tree cover. They include savannas, temperate prairies, steppes, and natural grasslands, depending on the region and climate.

In the Amazonian and South American context, they encompass both natural grasslands (such as the Llanos de Moxos or the Roraima savanna) and semi-natural areas derived from livestock use or periodic burning. Grasslands store large amounts of carbon in soil and underground biomass; their degradation or conversion releases that carbon into the atmosphere. They host high diversity of herbaceous species, birds, and pollinators, including endemic and migratory species, and constitute crucial habitats for savanna and steppe fauna. They support traditional systems of extensive livestock farming, grazing, and family agriculture, essential for food security and rural culture. Well-conserved grasslands reduce erosion and increase water infiltration, promoting resilience to droughts and preventing desertification.

### Data Source and Processing

This layer is a proprietary compilation by AmazoniaForever360+, 2024, based on the Global Pasture Watch – Annual Grassland Class and Extent Maps (2000–2024). The source file `gpw_grassland_rf.med.filt.bthr_c_30m_AMAZ_v2.tif` was generalized by aggregation to 250m using the majority value per pixel criterion.

### Classification

The attribute table includes four classes:

- **0 – Other land cover**: surfaces that do not correspond to grasslands (forests, water bodies, urban areas, etc.)
- **1 – Cultivated grassland**: planted or intensively managed grasslands for livestock or agricultural production
- **2 – Natural/Semi-natural grassland**: prairies and savannas of natural or semi-natural origin, with dominant herbaceous vegetation
- **3 – Open shrubland**: areas of open scrubland or transitional between grassland and low woody vegetation

### About Global Pasture Watch

The Global Pasture Watch – Annual Grassland Class and Extent Maps (2000–2024) is a global dataset showing the distribution and annual changes in the extent of natural, semi-natural, and cultivated grasslands worldwide between 2000 and 2024, with a spatial resolution of 30 meters. It was developed by Liu et al. (2024) through time-series analysis of Landsat and Sentinel-2 imagery, processed with deep learning models capable of distinguishing herbaceous vegetation-dominated areas from other land covers.

The dataset allows evaluation of the spatio-temporal dynamics of grasslands, including their conversion to agricultural uses or recovery, and serves as a key input for biodiversity studies, carbon balance, sustainable livestock management, and open ecosystem restoration.

### Data Access

- Public data available through Zenodo (GeoTIFF format, global coverage): https://zenodo.org/records/15648751
- Accessible in Google Earth Engine as 'Global Pasture Watch' with annual maps of dominant grassland classes at 30m
- Additional grassland and non-forest vegetation data: https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/publisher/global-pasture-watch

### References

- Parente, L., Liu, Y., & Gong, P. (2024). Annual 30-m maps of global grassland class and extent. *Scientific Data* (Nature Publishing Group). DOI: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-024-04139-6
- Lu, Y., Liu, S., Zhang, H., & Wang, J. (2022). Review of Remote Sensing Applications in Grassland Monitoring. *Remote Sensing*, 14(12), 2903. DOI: https://doi.org/10.3390/rs14122903

indicators.name: Canopy height
indicators.description:
## Amazon Canopy Height Layer (2020–2024)

Raster layer representing an estimate of canopy height, which is the upper layer of trees, sampled at 250m pixels. Tree crowns intercept most sunlight and regulate the exchange of energy, water, and gases between the ecosystem and the atmosphere. Their structure, height, density, and composition reflect the ecological maturity of the forest and its capacity to store carbon.

In the context of sustainable development planning and management, canopy height is a key indicator of ecological integrity and biological productivity. Forests with tall, closed canopies tend to have greater aboveground biomass, meaning plant material (foliage, branches), making them critical carbon reservoirs and essential elements for climate change mitigation. Additionally, the canopy creates a stable microclimate that sustains high species diversity, protects soils from erosion, and maintains regional water flows.

### Data Source and Processing

This layer is a proprietary compilation by AmazoniaForever360+, 2024, based on the Amazon Canopy Height Dataset (2020-2024) published by CTrees organization. This extremely detailed raster model provides 22,063 tiles, each representing the average height of tree crowns in the Amazon rainforest, with a spatial resolution of 4.78 meters. The tiles, each covered by a .tif file, were downloaded and hosted in a virtual mosaic in ArcGIS Pro, from which a simplified clustering generalization tool was used to average canopy heights into 250m pixels.

### About CTrees

CTrees is an international scientific initiative dedicated to forest monitoring through satellite observations and advanced modeling techniques. Its objective is to estimate, with high resolution and methodological transparency, the amount of carbon stored in forest biomass and the changes it experiences over time.

CTrees data primarily come from LiDAR measurements obtained by the GEDI (Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation) and ICESat-2 missions, complemented with optical and radar information and processed through machine learning algorithms that allow extrapolation of tree canopy height at global scale.

The Global Canopy Height Dataset (2020–2024) offers maps of average canopy height expressed in meters above ground. In CTrees classification, tree canopy is considered to be any vegetation with a minimum approximate height of 5 meters, so values below that threshold typically correspond to shrublands, savannas, or open areas without significant forest cover.

### Data Access

- Original data in GeoTIFF format and WGS84 projection (EPSG:4326) publicly available through AWS Open Data program: https://registry.opendata.aws/ctrees/

### References

- Amazon Web Services (AWS). (2023). CTrees uses AWS to track carbon in every living tree on Earth. *Amazon Web Services Public Sector Blog*. Available at: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/publicsector/ctrees-uses-aws-to-track-carbon-in-every-living-tree-on-earth/
- Lang, N., Schindler, K., Wegner, J. D., et al. (2023). A high-resolution canopy height model of the Earth. *Nature Ecology & Evolution*, 7, 1403–1412. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41559-023-02206-6
